question: Test whether re-encoding preserves incoming answer content despite changing private context, and whether empirical cross/self trajectories exhibit semantic parity rather than generic degradation.
conditions: One cross trajectory and one self trajectory per item, retaining both agents endpoints at rounds0..6.
The four common-input cells G_i(m_j_initial) are already produced by cross/self round1; reuse them when numerical equivalence is established.
Compare each pair G0(m_j) vsG1(m_j) under the same downstream receiver D0. Two of four final readings already occur at cross/self round2; only two additional passes are needed for the other pair.
stop_rules: If cross/self neural answer trajectories show no reproducible odd/even contrast, reject parity-specific explanation; do not keep tuning round choices.

If equal incoming messages produce strongly context-dependent, functionally distinct outgoing messages, the shared-map approximation is not supported; seek another explanation for endpoint self resemblance.
Agreement on two initial-message inputs cannot establish a global Lipschitz bound or equality on hybrid trajectories. Do not promote the conditional mathematical bound to a neural result.
If new trajectories only show generic answer copying already covered by prior art, do not present it as a new paper-level mechanism.
